speaker: narrator
text: Act III: Trials and Revelations

speaker: narrator
text: You said it aloud in the castle courtyard, with the vision still fading: “He took them. That is why they vanished, and that is why he wants me.” Sir Cedric did not correct you. Nobody has, and so it has become what you believe: Malakar took your parents, and now he is coming for you.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira came to Greendale the night of the vision. She had felt the amulet open to the forest, she said, and knew. In the castle courtyard she drew a circle in chalk, and the three of you stepped out of it into her hut in Willowbrook, the herbs still swinging from the beam. She has not yet said how a village healer learned to do that.

speaker: narrator
text: Now she is the only one who can say what must be done next, and where the road to Malakar begins.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira's Hut

speaker: narrator
text: A small hut hung with drying herbs: lavender, sage, and roots in bundles from the rafters. Shelves of bottles line the walls, every one labelled. Mira moves among them without looking, the way you cross your own kitchen in the dark.

speaker: narrator
text: Bundles of resin-sweet stems and silverleaf—Mira's blends for steadying wounds and sharpening ritual focus during complex workings.

speaker: narrator
text: Reflections in the prism hover a breath out of sync—each a doorway waiting for Mira's word.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre is the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn: the sun rising over three linked rings. It is faintly warm in your hand.

speaker: mira
text: Elior. Malakar is draining the life out of King Alden, and the king grows weaker every day.

speaker: mira
text: Three relics can stand against him: the crystal of light, the phoenix feather and the dragon's scale. We will fetch them one at a time.

speaker: mira
text: Before we go, take this, and read it.

speaker: narrator
text: She puts a small, worn piece of parchment in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a keepsake note.

speaker: mira
text: Tell me when you are ready, and I will draw the first circle.

speaker: mira
text: On the road, ask me what you need to. I may not be able to answer all of it yet.

speaker: narrator
text: (Ask her with: say parents, say malakar, say amulet or say grandmother to Mira.)

speaker: sir cedric
text: Go and speak with Mira. She knows where we go from here. I will be beside you when we get there.

speaker: narrator
text: The village healer, with chalk dust still on her sleeves from the circle in the castle yard. She watches you the way she watches a fever.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall knight in old, dented mail, his sword at his hip again. He keeps half a step behind you and to one side, where a guard walks.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around Mira's Hut, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: You think it over. Nothing presses on you just now.

speaker: narrator
text: You rest for a moment, gathering your strength.

speaker: mira
text: You should read the note I gave you first, Elior. I wrote it for the road, and I want it read before we go.

speaker: narrator
text: New main quest

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues

speaker: narrator
text: Mira says Malakar is draining the life out of King Alden. Three relics can stand against him: the crystal of light, the phoenix feather and the dragon's scale.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior. The people who made the relics left words behind them: by the sea, on the mountain and under the hills. Keep your eyes open for traces of the past. Read what they left, all of it, before you judge anyone.

speaker: narrator
text: She has underlined the last line twice.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Mira knows the way. I know how to stand in front of you. Between us, that will have to do.

speaker: narrator
text: You stop and think over what you know.

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues: Mira says Malakar is draining the life out of King Alden. Three relics can stand against him: the crystal of light, the phoenix feather and the dragon's scale.

speaker: narrator
text: New side quest

speaker: narrator
text: Echoes of the Hidden Bond

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents made the three relics, long before you were born. Mira says they left words behind them: by the sea, on the mountain and under the hills.

speaker: narrator
text: By the sea: something they left in the Sunken Ruins.

speaker: narrator
text: On the mountain: something they left on Mount Ember.

speaker: narrator
text: Under the hills: something they left in the Caverns of Shadow.

speaker: mira
text: Then we go. The first circle sets us down on the Tidal Causeway, by the Sunken Ruins.

speaker: mira
text: When the air folds and the mist closes, breathe. It will pass in a heartbeat.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira traces a prism in the air with one finger. The air folds and the world blurs, and when it clears, the air smells different.

speaker: narrator
text: Echoes of the Hidden Bond: Your parents made the three relics, long before you were born. Mira says they left words behind them: by the sea, on the mountain and under the hills. By the sea: something they left in the Sunken Ruins.

speaker: mira
text: The crystal of light is somewhere in these ruins. It answers to courage. It parts veils and steadies the spirit. When you stand before the tide-born guardian, speak your vow, and mean it.

speaker: narrator
text: Tidal Causeway

speaker: narrator
text: Thin causeways of old stone run out across the black water. The wet stones shine under the moon. Broken arches stand along the way, and their shadows lie deep over a faded mural.

speaker: narrator
text: Fine salt lines run along the mural's base. Pressing the stone, your hand finds a hollow and a dry scrap falls into your palm. A sea-sealed letter peels free, its ink half-hidden by varnish made of salt and tide.

speaker: narrator
text: A jagged remnant of timber studded with barnacles. It juts from the pier, more anchor than object.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Salt and old stone. Give me a wall to hold and I would know what to do. Here I just follow you.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Tidal Causeway, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The two figures still shield the child, and the third still reaches toward them. Where a small box was sealed into the paint, empty stone now shows its place.

speaker: narrator
text: The letter's ink, protected by crystalline varnish, is still clear:

speaker: mother
text: Malakar, our friend —

speaker: mother
text: We made the relics together, the three of us, and swore they would only ever guard, never take. Now you speak of time as if it were a door you could open and close again. It is not a door. It is a wound, and what comes through it will not stop at saving us.

speaker: mother
text: We are not afraid of what is coming. We are afraid of what you will become to stop it. Wait with us. Be patient, for once. If you will not, we will stand against you, not as your enemies but as your friends, and as Wardens of the Dawn.

speaker: mother
text: — Aren and Lysa

speaker: narrator
text: Beneath their names, in a sharper hand and darker ink, someone has written a reply:

speaker: malakar
text: You would have me wait while you die. — M.

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents wrote to Malakar as a friend. He read it, and answered.

speaker: narrator
text: At your side, the ancient amulet grows warm, then glows. In its light you glimpse two faces, a man and a woman, laughing beside a third figure who has turned away. Then the light fades.

speaker: narrator
text: Out past the arches the tide turns, and the surf that breaks on the causeway runs grey. Dead sea birds lie along the stones, more than you can count, their feathers dull with salt. Whatever is draining the king is draining the sea as well.

speaker: mira
text: Lysa's hand. She always crossed her sevens.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira turns to the sea before you can ask what she means.

speaker: narrator
text: You carefully fold the letter — a plea to a friend, kept by the sea.

speaker: narrator
text: Echoes of the Hidden Bond: Your parents made the three relics, long before you were born. Mira says they left words behind them: by the sea, on the mountain and under the hills. By the sea: the letter you found in the Sunken Ruins. You have not read it yet.

speaker: narrator
text: Quest updated

speaker: narrator
text: In the Sunken Ruins: a letter from Aren and Lysa to their friend Malakar, begging him not to reach for time. He wrote back: You would have me wait while you die.

speaker: narrator
text: Shoreline Markers

speaker: narrator
text: Weathered steles stand in the cold sand, their faces full of shallow marks. Salt has smudged most of the lines, but moon sigils still show when the tide drops. Pale flakes sit loose in the grooves and catch the light.

speaker: narrator
text: You brush aside kelp and barnacle crusts. A cluster of pale moon shards comes free—etched with curved lines that seem to hum when the moon leans toward the sea. They feel keyed to the tide, as if the lunar pull listens to these marks.

speaker: narrator
text: Tideward Sigils

speaker: narrator
text: Three warding pillars stand in the drowned courtyard of the Outer Wards. Cleaned and set with moon sigils, they could draw the sea back from the hall beyond.

speaker: narrator
text: The shards whisper with tide-salt; they leave a faint dust on your fingers.

speaker: narrator
text: Outer Wards

speaker: narrator
text: The courtyard lies half under the sea. Three old pillars rise from the black water, their faces scored with shallow marks. Brine beads along the carved lines and catches the moon in small rings of light.

speaker: narrator
text: You rinse salt and scrape coral from the carved channels. Glyph-lines breathe again, ready to take the Tideward Sigil.

speaker: narrator
text: You press the pale shards into the cleansed grooves. Pale runes flare and sink into the stone like stored moonlight. The air leans in; a pull runs through the courtyard as the tide answers the sigils, and the sea draws back from the drowned hall to the south.

speaker: narrator
text: Side quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: You cleansed the pillars and set the Moon Rune shards—the Moon Sigil resonates and the flood wards steady, granting safe passage toward the sanctum.

speaker: narrator
text: Collapsed Pier

speaker: narrator
text: The pier has fallen into the tide. Warped planks gape over dark vaults, and barnacled timbers stand up out of the water. The sea knocks against them, slow and steady.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden nods slowly.

speaker: pier warden
text: You've done right by the pillars. There's a fused locker down in the vaults; I tried a key once but it stuck. Key's no good alone, and magic's no good alone. It wants both. Lost that key after, in some dark hole by the mural on the causeway. You'd want a light to find it.

speaker: pier warden
text: You'll have seen the causeway. Birds by the hundred, and the surf gone grey. I've known bad seasons on this coast, forty years of them. It's only a bad season, isn't it? Tell me the sea will mend on its own.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre is the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn: the sun rising over three linked rings. In its depths two faces linger: a man and a woman, laughing beside a third figure who has turned away.

speaker: narrator
text: Echoes of the Hidden Bond: Your parents made the three relics, long before you were born. Mira says they left words behind them: by the sea, on the mountain and under the hills. On the mountain: something they left on Mount Ember.

speaker: narrator
text: Thin causeways of old stone run out across the black water. The wet stones shine under the moon. Broken arches stand along the way, and their shadows lie deep over a faded mural. Dead sea birds line the stones, and the surf runs grey.

speaker: narrator
text: Your light catches a patch of pigment and a small hollow. In the shadowed cranny, something metallic flakes free — a corroded key rests in the rock.

speaker: narrator
text: A corroded iron key from a hollow in the causeway rock, beside the mural. Its teeth are pitted with salt and age.

speaker: narrator
text: The key's teeth are ragged with corrosion; it might fit, but the lock has long since fused.

speaker: narrator
text: The steles bear shallow moon-marks, pores packed with salt. Loose pale fragments glint in crevices—likely usable in sigil work.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, iridescent shell smoothed by long tides. It's pretty and shines in the moonlight. Held to your ear, it seems to hum.

speaker: narrator
text: Thin, chalky shards veined with pale luster. Each shard holds a faint lunar marking, as if carved in moonlight and salt.

speaker: narrator
text: Tideward Sigils: Three warding pillars stand in the drowned courtyard of the Outer Wards. Cleaned and set with moon sigils, they could draw the sea back from the hall beyond.

speaker: narrator
text: The pillars stand mute in the dim, their faces ringed with crust and shadow. A faint, weary hum hides under the stone, a thread of old magic barely holding. They watch the water but do not command it.

speaker: narrator
text: A dense mat of seaweed clings to the stones, slick and knotted. It seems rooted to the surf.

speaker: narrator
text: Apart from the three warding pillars rising from the black water, the drowned courtyard holds little of interest; the pillars alone seem keyed to the moon and tide.

speaker: narrator
text: The pillars pulse with a quiet, radiant rhythm. Light seems to gather in the carved channels, a steady heartbeat that draws the tide toward the stone. The air tastes of moonwater; the ward answers, ready to pull the sea back when the sigil is set.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden squints at the key.

speaker: pier warden
text: Found my old key, did you? It'll stick in that lock, same as it did for me. Key's no good alone, and magic's no good alone.

speaker: elior
text: truth

speaker: narrator
text: You tell the Pier Warden what you know: this is no season. Something is draining the king, and the sea with him, and it is getting worse.

speaker: pier warden
text: … Aye. I think I knew it. I only wanted someone to tell me otherwise. I'll send word up the coast to keep the boats in.

speaker: pier warden
text: I've sent word up the coast. The boats are staying in.

speaker: narrator
text: This might come in handy, so you decide to pick it up.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden turns the coin over once, then folds your fingers back around it.

speaker: pier warden
text: Keep it. Toll for the crossing, my da said.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden pushes your hand away.

speaker: pier warden
text: I said keep it, lad.

speaker: elior
text: yes

speaker: pier warden
text: Aye. That's what I'll tell the boats, then.

speaker: narrator
text: He goes back to watching the water.

speaker: pier warden
text: A bad season, you said. That's what I've told the boats.

speaker: narrator
text: Barnacles crust the seam; the fused lock will not yield to a mundane key.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, greened coin whose face has long since been worn away. It might be worth something to a collector, but not here.

speaker: narrator
text: An old man in a salt-stiff coat, sitting on the last sound plank of the jetty with his eyes on the water.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Collapsed Pier, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: pier warden
text: Nothing to say? Then it's a bad season, and it'll pass. It always has.

speaker: narrator
text: The lock is too corroded for the key to turn. As you tug, the corroded key jams in the mechanism and will not come free.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden laughs, short.

speaker: pier warden
text: Stuck fast, is it? Same as mine was. Key's no good alone, and magic's no good alone.

speaker: narrator
text: A subtle click echoes under the pier as fused pins release. The locker can now be opened.

speaker: narrator
text: The mechanism is freed; the door can be opened.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden cocks his head toward the vaults.

speaker: pier warden
text: That's the click I never got. Go on, then; it's yours.

speaker: narrator
text: With a brittle crack the door gives, revealing three prism lanterns gleaming behind veils of silt.

speaker: narrator
text: The door hangs open and the interior is still and cold, silt motes drifting inside.

speaker: narrator
text: A faceted lantern of glass ribs and brass, made to scatter light into clear paths.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden looks at the open locker.

speaker: pier warden
text: Forty years that locker was shut. Those lanterns hung in the deeps once, my da said, where the light never gets.

speaker: narrator
text: Submerged Antechamber

speaker: narrator
text: The tide has drawn back, and the water in the hall is low and cold. Salt crystals glitter on the stone it left bare, and niches stand open along the carved walls. The air is colder, and your steps echo.

speaker: narrator
text: You wade through chilled water. As you peer into the niches, three carved brackets become apparent; their grooves catch the faint tide-light.

speaker: narrator
text: Lanterns of the Deeps

speaker: narrator
text: Three carved brackets line the flooded antechamber, cut to hold a lantern. With a light burning in each, the hall might show the way through.

speaker: narrator
text: An empty bracket waits for a lantern.

speaker: narrator
text: You wade through chilled water. Three empty brackets line the approach; their carved grooves catch the faint tide-light.

speaker: narrator
text: Lanterns of the Deeps: Three carved brackets line the flooded antechamber, cut to hold a lantern. With a light burning in each, the hall might show the way through.

speaker: narrator
text: The prism lantern settles into the bracket; water hums softly as it takes the weight.

speaker: narrator
text: A prism lantern rests here, ready to be lit.

speaker: narrator
text: You wade through chilled water. A prism lantern sits in one bracket; the other two stand empty, their grooves catching the faint tide-light.

speaker: narrator
text: You wade through chilled water. Prism lanterns sit in two of the brackets; the third stands empty, its grooves catching the faint tide-light.

speaker: narrator
text: You wade through chilled water. All three brackets hold prism lanterns, still unlit.

speaker: narrator
text: Light pours from the prisms, weaving a clear path through the flooded hall. The way to the sanctum stands revealed.

speaker: narrator
text: The prism lanterns burn in their brackets, and their light lays a clear path through the flooded hall to the sanctum.

speaker: narrator
text: The niches glow with steady, pearlescent flame. The lanterns you set here still burn.

speaker: narrator
text: A vaulted chamber floored with still, dark water. Sigils show on its surface and shift as you look at them, and pale motes of light drift on the ripples. At the room's heart a shallow basin holds a cold brightness; the air tastes of brine and vows left unsaid.

speaker: narrator
text: Then every light goes out at once — the sigils, the motes, the glow at your back. The Tide-Born Guardian speaks from the black:

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: The lanterns brought you here. They will not take you further. Walk.

speaker: narrator
text: Sanctum of the Tide

speaker: narrator
text: You stand at the edge of the black water. Somewhere ahead, the Tide-Born Guardian waits.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: Walk east into the water. When you come through, I will ask you one thing.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Water I cannot fight. I will keep the door, then. Better than I kept the last one.

speaker: narrator
text: A shape of standing water the height of a man. Ward-sigils drift in it like weed in a current.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Sanctum of the Tide, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: You step down into the black water. It is cold to the knees, and you cannot see your own hands.

speaker: narrator
text: Black water to your knees. You cannot see your own hands.

speaker: narrator
text: The water climbs to your waist. Then a voice like Mira's, close behind you:

speaker: mira
text: Turn back, Elior. There is nothing out there.

speaker: narrator
text: Black water to your waist. You cannot see your own hands.

speaker: narrator
text: The water is at your chest. You call for Sir Cedric. Nothing comes back. You take the step anyway.

speaker: narrator
text: The water parts around you. In the hollow it leaves, the crystal of light burns in its basin, the only light in the world.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: You came through. What did you not abandon?

speaker: narrator
text: A prism the size of your palm, cold and clear. Light moves in it like water under a moon.

speaker: narrator
text: The water stands parted around you. The crystal of light burns in its basin, the only light in the world.

speaker: elior
text: myself

speaker: narrator
text: The water draws back from you, all the way to the walls. The crystal of light sits loose in its basin.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: Most name a person, and leave themselves behind in the dark. You walked in whole, and you walked out whole.

speaker: narrator
text: One by one the sigils kindle again across the water, and the chamber is lit as you first saw it.

speaker: narrator
text: The Tide-Born Guardian turns its rippling face to Sir Cedric.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: Name what you will not abandon.

speaker: sir cedric
text: My king.

speaker: narrator
text: A breath.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I did once.

speaker: narrator
text: The water does not answer him.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: One came before you, long ago. Aren. He asked me to test whoever came after him the way he was tested.

speaker: sir cedric
text: It asked me, too. You heard my answer. So did the water, and it said nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystal is cold, and steady in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: You walked into the black water and named what you did not abandon: yourself. The guardian gave you the crystal of light. Sir Cedric has said little since it asked him the same question.

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues: You walked into the black water and named what you did not abandon: yourself. The guardian gave you the crystal of light. Sir Cedric has said little since it asked him the same question.

speaker: mira
text: Not yet, Elior. That letter in your bag was left for you, and you have not read it. I will not take you up the mountain until you have.

speaker: mira
text: Not yet, Elior. There is something in these ruins that was left for you. I will not take you up the mountain without it.

speaker: mira
text: That is one. Next is the mountain. The circle comes down on the Lower Switchbacks, where the path climbs over black glass and the wind carries ash. Keep your footing.

speaker: mira
text: And Elior. I can feel the king through the circle. He is weaker than when we set out.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric looks away, toward the mountain.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I had the wall that night. I heard nothing. Every day he is weaker, I hear it.

speaker: mira
text: A phoenix nests at the top of this mountain, where the rock is hottest. Only it can give the feather, and it asks for wisdom. The scholar camped on this path has read these slopes for years; start with him. And Elior: this mountain will not be hurried.

speaker: narrator
text: Lower Switchbacks

speaker: narrator
text: Paths wind back and forth across black, glassy rock, and ash blows on the wind. In the lee of the slope stands a scholar's camp: soot-patched canvas, low braziers, and racks where scorched notes and scraps of map flap. A workbench holds polishing stones and brass fittings for mending mirror segments, the kind found among the outcrops. Above the camp the slope climbs into obsidian, and vents hiss farther off.

speaker: narrator
text: The canteen's lining is scorched and patched; someone once used it to carry boiled ash and broth between camps. A folded scrap of brass is stitched into the seam — a useful fragment for repairing a mirror. You pry free a brass mirror segment from the lining; it falls to the ground nearby.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ash Scholar looks up from a tray of brass fittings and wipes the soot from both hands before speaking.

speaker: ash scholar
text: We are on an expedition: a small band of scholars and tinkerers, tracing the terraces and cataloguing anything that glints.

speaker: ash scholar
text: I found this brass mirror segment while prying at a collapsed ledge. It is small, but it will mend a mount. There will be more among the outcrops, if you search carefully.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a brass mirror segment.

speaker: ash scholar
text: This was in the same ledge. A notebook, burned nearly through. Whoever wrote in it knew these mirrors better than any of us, and I cannot make out who that was. Perhaps you can.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a charred notebook.

speaker: sir cedric
text: We stand about reading vents while he fades. Let me go through that heat first and see what it does.

speaker: narrator
text: A scholar in soot-streaked robes, with a sheaf of notes on mirror angles tied to one wrist so the wind cannot take it.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Lower Switchbacks, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ash Scholar taps a page of notes.

speaker: ash scholar
text: The mount on the terraces takes four segments, by my notes. Seek the outcrops for what the mountain has shed.

speaker: narrator
text: A battered brass segment whose face still catches light. It looks fragile but usable when bound into the mirror mounts.

speaker: narrator
text: Most of the notebook's pages have crumbled to flakes; two survive, in a neat and patient hand.

speaker: malakar
text: Lysa says I measure the light too carefully. Aren says that is why it never misses. We set the third mirror today, and the whole terrace caught fire with it, the good kind.

speaker: malakar
text: The Wasting has reached Willowbrook. Lysa coughs at night and pretends she does not. Aren sits up with her and pretends he is not afraid. They tell me to wait. I have waited all my life.

speaker: narrator
text: The second entry is pressed so hard into the page that the pen has torn it. The names in it are your parents'.

speaker: mira
text: You have his notes now; the slopes above are yours to read. And Elior: this mountain will not be hurried.

speaker: narrator
text: The canteen's lining is scorched and patched; someone once used it to carry boiled ash and broth between camps. A folded scrap of brass is stitched into the seam — a useful fragment for repairing a mirror.

speaker: narrator
text: Obsidian Outcrops

speaker: narrator
text: Sharp towers of obsidian stand up out of the ash, their faces split into glassy facets. In the seams between them lie weathered mirror fragments and the marks of old mounts: brass filings and small bolt holes. Glass flakes slide away under every step.

speaker: narrator
text: You pry at a narrow seam and a brass segment flakes free, along with a hardened pot of binding resin—useful for securing the mirror mounts.

speaker: narrator
text: A sticky, heat-cured resin used by mirrorwrights to bind brass segments into place.

speaker: narrator
text: Mirrors of Emberlight

speaker: narrator
text: The terraces are lined with old, cracked mirrors. Find a way to repair the mirrors and restore the channel of light to the high altar.

speaker: narrator
text: Mirror Terraces

speaker: narrator
text: Stepped platforms rise in rings up the slope, each ring set with sockets for mirrors and brass mounts. Channels cut in the stone carry light from ring to ring, toward the mountainside. Ash has settled on the worktables, over files and polish left where someone put them down.

speaker: narrator
text: You sift the ash and grit beneath the mount and find a brass mirror segment, half-buried in the sand.

speaker: narrator
text: You trace the charred letters with your finger. Above the words, cut shallow, is the sun over three rings; beneath it, older and nearly gone, a tree under two moons. The inscription reads:

speaker: narrator
text: We are three, and we are one promise.

speaker: father
text: I, Aren, pour courage into the crystal of light.

speaker: mother
text: I, Lysa, pour selflessness into the dragon's scale.

speaker: malakar
text: I, Malakar, pour wisdom into the phoenix feather.

speaker: narrator
text: What we pour into the ward, the ward will keep.

speaker: narrator
text: The last name is burned deeper than the others, as if the stone was struck again long after it cooled. Your parents and Malakar made this promise together, and the wisdom was his.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient amulet glows again, brighter than before, and the faces sharpen. The woman has Grandmother's eyes. She can only be Lysa, your mother. The third figure still has his back turned.

speaker: narrator
text: Ash begins to fall over the slopes, slow and grey as rain. Down the mountain the braziers gutter one by one and sink to embers. The curse lies heavier here than it did by the sea.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Mirror Terraces, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Mirrors of Emberlight: The terraces are lined with old, cracked mirrors. Find a way to repair the mirrors and restore the channel of light to the high altar.

speaker: narrator
text: On Mount Ember: the promise the three of them burned into stone, one virtue each, and Malakar's name struck deeper than the others.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre is the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn: the sun rising over three linked rings. In its depths the woman's face is clear: Lysa, with Grandmother's eyes. The man laughs beside her, and the third figure keeps his back turned.

speaker: narrator
text: Echoes of the Hidden Bond: Your parents made the three relics, long before you were born. Mira says they left words behind them: by the sea, on the mountain and under the hills. Under the hills: something they left in the Caverns of Shadow.

speaker: narrator
text: Stepped platforms rise in rings up the slope, each ring set with sockets for mirrors and brass mounts. Channels cut in the stone carry light from ring to ring, toward the mountainside. Ash has settled on the worktables, over files and polish left where someone put them down. Ash falls over the terraces like slow grey rain, and down the slope the braziers have guttered to embers.

speaker: narrator
text: A brass-and-stone mount fixed into the terrace socket. It needs a brass segment and binding resin to secure and repair the mirror face.

speaker: narrator
text: With a careful, ringing press you seat the brass segments and secure their alignment. The terrace mount accepts the fittings.

speaker: narrator
text: Four brass segments sit in the mount, but the seams between them are loose.

speaker: narrator
text: You apply the binding resin carefully around the seams; the brass segments sit firmer and the joints set.

speaker: narrator
text: Four brass segments sit in the mount, the resin set hard along their seams. The face holds together, but it is not yet whole.

speaker: narrator
text: A whispered mend gathers in your hands and the mirrors answer — seams knit, polish brightens, and the whole face hums.

speaker: narrator
text: The mirrors are whole. The sun is not where it needs to be. Perhaps rest a while, and let it climb.

speaker: narrator
text: The deeper cut fills. Malakar's name sits level with your parents' again, as it was the day they wrote it.

speaker: narrator
text: Stepped platforms rise in rings up the slope, each ring set with sockets for mirrors and brass mounts. Channels cut in the stone carry light from ring to ring, toward the mountainside. Ash has settled on the worktables, over files and polish left where someone put them down. The mended mirrors stand ready, their bright faces still waiting on the sun. Ash falls over the terraces like slow grey rain, and down the slope the braziers have guttered to embers.

speaker: narrator
text: The three names sit level and whole. There is nothing left to mend.

speaker: narrator
text: You settle on the warm stone and let the hours pass. The sun climbs until it stands squarely over the terraces. The great mirror catches it and throws one beam into the mountainside. Something gives inside the rock, and a narrow passage grinds open to the east.

speaker: narrator
text: You gathered the brass mirror segments, mended the mount on the terraces, and let the noon sun fire the beam that opened the way into the mountain.

speaker: narrator
text: Ember Gallery

speaker: narrator
text: A vaulted cavern veined with cooling lava; the air smells of charcoal and iron. Steam rises from cracks in the floor. On the worktables, fireglass and cooled slag lie sorted into heaps for wards, as if whoever sorted them meant to come back.

speaker: narrator
text: You sift through the sorted fragments on the worktable and find a brittle frond of ash-fern tucked in a tool roll, and a pile of cooled slag fragments sifted into a shallow basin. They look suitable for warding mixtures.

speaker: narrator
text: The ash-fern and cooled slag grind down into a coarse paste: a heat-ward mix.

speaker: narrator
text: Breath of the Mountain

speaker: narrator
text: The Fumarole Passages exhale waves of heat and steam, blocking the way forward. Find a way to cross the shifting vents and reach the heights to the south.

speaker: narrator
text: Fumarole Passages

speaker: narrator
text: Narrow tunnels breathe heat in and out through vents in the stone, the way a sleeper breathes. Steam hangs in the low passages, and the air smells of sulfur and warm metal. Small holes and rubbed brass in the floor show where mounts were once bolted.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents gust and sputter without rhythm; there is no telling when they will breathe next.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents click and a rhythmic hiss grows steadier—the timing seems closer to being synchronized.

speaker: narrator
text: With a final fit, the vents' rhythms align into a deep, slow breath. You sense the passages will now accept a heat ward to steady the crossing intervals.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents breathe together now, deep and slow, but every breath comes up hot enough to blister.

speaker: narrator
text: The rock grows a touch cooler around your hands as the ward seals into place. Down the tunnel you notice the gusting heat flatten into a steady breath—passage through the fumaroles is now safe for a short interval. The wild gusting settles into a slow, even breath: out, a held pause, and in. Each time it draws in, a cool draught runs south.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents exhale. A scalding gust roars up out of the southern tunnel.

speaker: narrator
text: You stand still and count.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents fall still, holding their breath. The heat hangs heavy and unmoving.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents draw in. A cool draught tugs past you toward the south.

speaker: narrator
text: You walk with the draught at your back, down through the cooling tunnel, and out beneath the open sky of the crater.

speaker: narrator
text: You set the vent stones, sealed the vents with ash-fern and slag, counted the mountain's breath, and crossed to the crater on the in-breath.

speaker: narrator
text: Phoenix Crater

speaker: narrator
text: A bowl of rock melted to glass, open to the sky. Warm drafts turn in it and carry cinders round in slow spirals. The air smells of hot iron. The warmth is drowsy here, as if the bowl would rather you sat and rested a while.

speaker: narrator
text: As your eyes close, the air grows warmer. When you open them, a phoenix is lying in the crater with you, watching you as if it has been there all along.

speaker: narrator
text: A bowl of rock melted to glass, open to the sky. Warm drafts turn in it and carry cinders round in slow spirals. The air smells of hot iron. At the crater's heart the phoenix lies on a bed of cooled slag, its feathers red-gold and steaming. Each breath it lets out sends sparks up out of the bowl. Now and then a feather comes loose and cools on the rim to a shard that still hums.

speaker: narrator
text: The phoenix does not open its beak, but its voice is in your head all the same:

speaker: phoenix
text: What is wisdom when time is short?

speaker: narrator
text: It lets the question stand.

speaker: phoenix
text: I asked this once of the Warden of Wisdom, when he came to me with his two friends. He knew the answer, and did not keep it.

speaker: elior
text: patience

speaker: narrator
text: The phoenix bends its neck, draws a single feather from its breast and lays it in your hands.

speaker: phoenix
text: Wisdom is patience, even when the world burns. Take this, and remember.

speaker: phoenix
text: He gave your answer too. Then time grew short for his friends, and patience was the one thing he had none of. Do not become what he became.

speaker: narrator
text: You think of the third name on the terraces, level with the others again.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a phoenix feather.

speaker: narrator
text: Beside you, Sir Cedric looks at the ground.

speaker: narrator
text: You answered the phoenix: wisdom is patience, even when the world burns. It gave you a feather, and told you of a Warden who had none.

speaker: narrator
text: The phoenix inclines its head.

speaker: phoenix
text: You saw his name on the terraces, burned deeper than the others. No fire did that. He came back, years after, and struck it again himself, to cut himself out of the promise. The stone would not let him.

speaker: phoenix
text: You gave him back his place. He could not do that for himself.

speaker: phoenix
text: Remember him when time is short for you.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ash Scholar looks up toward the terraces.

speaker: ash scholar
text: The mirror on the terraces is burning again; I saw it catch from here. Four segments, as my notes said.

speaker: mira
text: The mirror on the terraces is lit; I saw it from here. The phoenix is higher still, past the heat. And Elior: this mountain will not be hurried.

speaker: narrator
text: The mirror sits whole and firm in its mount. Its seams have knit, and its face is bright.

speaker: narrator
text: A brittle frond blackened by the mountain's breath. When mixed with cooled slag it can form a rudimentary heat‑ward paste.

speaker: narrator
text: Rough, glassy fragments of slag cooled against the tunnel walls. When ground with ash-fern it forms a basic heat‑ward paste.

speaker: narrator
text: You search the Ember Gallery again but find nothing new beyond the worktables and sorted fragments.

speaker: narrator
text: A coarse paste of ash-fern and cooled slag prepared to seal and stabilize vent stones against the mountain's heat.

speaker: narrator
text: A smooth, heat-tempered stone carved with grooves that fit into the fumarole fittings. Several are needed to calibrate the vents.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents still gust out of time with each other. A ward laid on them now would crack at the first wrong breath.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric steps toward the vents; the heat drives him back a pace.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Between breaths, then. I have run through worse than this.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian studies you for a moment.

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: You have come for the Phoenix. Then you must be both patient and watchful. The vents breathe wild here, and the heat will turn you back. First bring the vents into harmony, so they breathe as one. Then bind the heat with a ward; the gallery below the terraces has what a ward is made of. When the rhythm is steady and the ward is set, the way to the crater opens.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall, masked figure in fire-etched robes stands by the vents, staff in hand. His head is turned to the vents, and his lips move as if he is counting.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Fumarole Passages, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Breath of the Mountain: The Fumarole Passages exhale waves of heat and steam, blocking the way forward. Find a way to cross the shifting vents and reach the heights to the south.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian listens to the vents.

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: They breathe as one now. Bind the heat with a ward, and they will hold.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian watches the vents.

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: The ward holds, but the mountain still breathes. Count its breath. Walk when it draws in.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian nods:

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: The way is open, but patience is your ally. The Phoenix will not appear for those who rush. Sit in the crater a while, and let it come to you.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Patience. The king has had nothing from us but patience.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Through the heat, and he is no stronger for it. The crater is yours. I will keep my hand off my sword.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Phoenix Crater, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: A phoenix the size of a cottage roof lies in the crater's glass. Its feathers go from gold to red as it breathes, and it watches you without any hurry.

speaker: narrator
text: The heat of the crater soaks into you, and the ache goes out of your legs.

speaker: narrator
text: You think of the third name burned deeper than the others on the terraces.

speaker: narrator
text: A single feather shed by the Phoenix, warm as a heartbeat, red at the quill and gold at the tip. It hums faintly in your hand.

speaker: sir cedric
text: A bird told us to wait, and we waited. I hope it was worth what it cost the king.

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues: You answered the phoenix: wisdom is patience, even when the world burns. It gave you a feather, and told you of a Warden who had none.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian lowers his staff.

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: It came to you, then. Few wait long enough for that. Go well.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ash Scholar stares at the feather in your hand.

speaker: ash scholar
text: We have catalogued everything on this mountain that glints, and never that. Keep it close. It is not for my notes.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira looks at the feather a long time.

speaker: mira
text: …even when the world burns.

speaker: narrator
text: She says it softly, before you have told her what the phoenix said.

speaker: mira
text: That is two. The last is under the hills. The circle comes down at the Cavern Mouth, and it is cold in there, colder than you think. Keep your coat on.

speaker: mira
text: There is a word the old folk will reach for when this ash comes down on them: the Wasting. It is not that. The Wasting killed. This drinks.

speaker: mira
text: The king is weaker still. Whatever drains him draws harder with every site we reach.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric's hand goes to his sword hilt and stays there.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Weaker still. And I stood on a mountain, waiting on a bird.

speaker: mira
text: There are miners trapped somewhere under this hill, Elior. Help them first. The way to the dragon goes through their galleries, and I would not walk past them if it did not.

speaker: narrator
text: Cavern Mouth

speaker: narrator
text: A broad arch opens into the hill, hung with cold mist. Lantern light dims a step inside it. Old signs are cut into the arch stone, worn too smooth to read.

speaker: narrator
text: The Mine Overseer grips your arm, voice hoarse:

speaker: mine overseer
text: The roof came down at dawn. Half a dozen men are trapped behind it. We dug, and the walls groaned at every blow, so we stopped. The young ones shouted for hours. Now there's nothing. Gods, let them still be alive.

speaker: narrator
text: He points north, jaw clenched:

speaker: mine overseer
text: The Tool Cache is up there: braces, straps, wedge blocks. The Collapsed Galleries are past it, east. Brace the roof before you touch the rock, or it comes down on you.

speaker: narrator
text: He presses a heavy iron key into your palm, his hand trembling:

speaker: mine overseer
text: Here—take my key. It opens the supply crate. Get those miners out.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive the miner's key.

speaker: sir cedric
text: People under the rock. That I understand. Point me at the heavy end.

speaker: narrator
text: A foreman in a coat grey with rock dust, a ring of keys at his belt. He keeps looking past you, into the dark.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Cavern Mouth, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Mine Overseer has not moved from the arch.

speaker: mine overseer
text: Still nothing from the galleries. The Tool Cache is north.

speaker: narrator
text: Miners' Rescue

speaker: narrator
text: Collapsed Galleries have trapped people behind tons of stone. You must find a way to free them.

speaker: narrator
text: A heavy iron key, pitted with age, used to open the supply crates.

speaker: narrator
text: Miners' Rescue: Collapsed Galleries have trapped people behind tons of stone. You must find a way to free them.

speaker: narrator
text: Tool Cache

speaker: narrator
text: A side chamber shored with old timbers and stacked with crates of braces, iron fittings and coils of hemp rope. The walls are scored with tool marks, and the air smells of iron and wet earth.

speaker: narrator
text: You search deeper into the shadowed alcove and discover a heavy supply crate hidden behind stacked timbers, locked with a large iron padlock that glints with an almost malevolent gleam. The label reads: 'Rescue Supplies — For Emergency Use Only.' The padlock is iron, rusted shut, and it has a keyhole.

speaker: narrator
text: The padlock is sturdy and rusted, but the keyhole looks intact. The crate is labeled for rescue supplies.

speaker: narrator
text: You've already found the heavy supply crate, locked with its large iron padlock. The label still reads: 'Rescue Supplies — For Emergency Use Only.'

speaker: narrator
text: With a click, the padlock opens. The crate is now unlocked. The miner's key is left twisted and useless, and you discard it.

speaker: narrator
text: The crate is unlocked but still closed. You could try to open it.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the crate are heavy iron braces, strong hemp straps and tapered wooden wedge blocks.

speaker: narrator
text: The crate stands open, its contents mostly removed.

speaker: narrator
text: Heavy iron braces used to shore up unstable rock walls.

speaker: narrator
text: Strong hemp straps for binding braces and hauling debris.

speaker: narrator
text: Tapered wooden blocks used to pry and stabilize fallen rock.

speaker: narrator
text: Collapsed Galleries

speaker: narrator
text: A gallery choked with fallen stone, floor to roof. The timbers that held it lie snapped under the pile, and dust hangs in the still air.

speaker: narrator
text: Loose stones hang over the pile, and the ceiling sags above them. Behind it the tapping goes on. Pull one stone now and the roof comes with it: it needs holding up first.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Collapsed Galleries, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The reinforced braces wedge under the sagging ceiling and steady the collapse. The immediate danger of further cave-in is reduced, but the braces need to be secured before you can safely clear the passage.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric takes the beam on his shoulder and holds it while you set it.

speaker: narrator
text: The support straps bind the reinforced braces securely, so they can withstand the pressure when the debris is cleared. The structure is now stable enough for the final excavation.

speaker: narrator
text: The wedge blocks bite into the cracks, and the pile gives way. Through the gap, grey with dust, the miners come out one at a time, blinking at your light.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric drives the last block home with the flat of his shield.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners gather around as the lead miner steps forward, dust-covered but relieved:

speaker: miners
text: Thank the gods you found us. Roof came down this morning and kept coming. We sat in the dark and listened to each other breathe.

speaker: narrator
text: Another miner adds, voice shaking:

speaker: miners
text: We heard you setting the braces. Every knock, we waited for the roof. It held.

speaker: narrator
text: The lead miner lowers his voice and nods toward a boy sitting apart from the rest:

speaker: miners
text: That's Tobin. Youngest of us. He was the one shouting for help, hours of it, till his voice went. Hasn't said a word since. Not one.

speaker: narrator
text: The lead miner wipes his hands on his shirt:

speaker: miners
text: We owe you, Elior. We'll stay and beam this section properly before anyone else comes through. The way east to the Echo Chambers is open, and we'll keep it open.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners are already reaching for the spare timbers.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric sets down the last beam and does not step away from it.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Someone should stay until the braces settle. I will.

speaker: narrator
text: The lead miner puts a grey hand on his arm.

speaker: lead miner
text: You have a king to fetch, ser. We have stood in worse holes than this one.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric looks down at the hand on his arm, then nods.

speaker: narrator
text: Half a dozen miners, grey with rock dust, passing timbers hand to hand. The oldest of them gives the orders, and nobody argues.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners look up from their work, tools in hand:

speaker: miners
text: Still here, Elior? Beams are going in. The way east to the Echo Chambers is sound. Go when you're ready.

speaker: narrator
text: The fallen stone is heaped along the walls now, and the gallery runs open end to end. The old timbers lie snapped among it.

speaker: narrator
text: You stabilized the collapse and led the miners to safety. The route to the inner caverns is now open.

speaker: sir cedric
text: They are out. The old man was right. I have a king to fetch.

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin looks at you for a long moment. His lips part, then close again. He turns the cracked lamp over in his hands and goes back to watching the ceiling.

speaker: narrator
text: A boy of perhaps fifteen sits apart from the others on an upturned bucket, knees drawn up, a cracked lamp in his lap. His throat is wrapped in a strip of torn shirt. He watches the ceiling, not you.

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin swallows, and you see what it costs him. No sound comes. He shakes his head, once.

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin does not look up. His thumb traces the crack in the lamp's glass, back and forth.

speaker: narrator
text: The runes describe a chant to quiet the phantoms: 'Let stillness echo, let silence bind.' You notice you could make rubbings of these ancient symbols.

speaker: narrator
text: Echo Chambers

speaker: narrator
text: Smooth caverns of bare stone. Every step comes back to you from the alcoves, and so does every word, a breath late, as if someone were copying you. Runes cover the walls, cut by three hands, the same words over and over.

speaker: narrator
text: Stillness Vestibule

speaker: narrator
text: A hush falls over this chamber like a shroud. Dark pools mirror the ceiling, so still they look frozen in time, and the stone seems to swallow every sound. At the centre, three weathered echo stones stand in a triangle. Their carved channels look made to catch whispered words and hold them.

speaker: narrator
text: As the blessing leaves your lips, the echo stones hum, and you feel it in your bones. Silver light runs along their carved channels like water finding its course. Then the light settles into a slow, steady glow.

speaker: narrator
text: The stones are warm now, and waiting for words.

speaker: narrator
text: Oath of Stillness

speaker: narrator
text: Grey figures drift among the pools of the Stillness Vestibule, saying the same thing over, as they have for years. The way to the dragon's hall stays shut until the echo stones there are blessed and given the old chant. Its words are cut into the walls of the Echo Chambers.

speaker: narrator
text: You unstopper the phial and let a single drop fall into the nearest pool. The ripple does not spread; it sinks, and the stillness goes down after it until the black water lies flat as glass, holding the stones and the dark above in perfect reflection.

speaker: narrator
text: The pools are mirror-still. Now the chant will carry.

speaker: narrator
text: You recite the resonant chant at each stone.

speaker: narrator
text: The words echo and re-echo, building into a silence that settles over the chamber. The phantoms stop where they stand, and fade into it. The path to the dragon's hall now lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: The chant ran through the echo stones and out across the still water, and the hush of the Stillness Vestibule closed over it. Nothing there is saying the same thing over any more, and the way to the dragon's hall lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: Dragon's Hall

speaker: narrator
text: A hall of living stone opens beyond sight, its ceiling lost in shadow. Embers burn slowly along the floor, pulsing like a heartbeat, and somewhere in the dark, water drips. Rings of old sigils spiral across the black tiles around the Ancient Dragon. It lies coiled at the centre, scales like polished obsidian, and each slow breath hums in your bones.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon opens one golden eye. Its voice is slow, and very low:

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Young one, I remember your parents. Aren and Lysa, Wardens of the Dawn. They came down here with their friend Malakar for a scale, the three of them laughing. They were making the relics together, as equals.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: When Malakar tore a wound in time, it was they who stood against him. They poured themselves into a ward. It hides you from his sight, and it holds his wound shut. It is anchored in the amulet you carry, and in the bindings of your king, who was their friend and gave his crown's oath to hold it. That is why Malakar drains him.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon is quiet for a long breath.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: They are warded away, not dead, child.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: They had a saying, the three of them, carved wherever they worked: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth. When he offers you what you want most, say it to him. It was his before it was yours.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient amulet blazes in your hand a third time. Aren stands beside Lysa now, hand in hand. Behind them, the third figure still has his back turned.

speaker: narrator
text: Far off in the mines the ring of picks stops, and does not start again. Then the cavern's old dripping stops too, and the silence is complete. The curse has reached even here, beneath the oldest hills.

speaker: narrator
text: Then, beneath the dragon's breathing, another voice: the whisper from your dream, at the very edge of hearing.

speaker: voice
text: Elior… little one. Help me. I cannot hold it shut alone.

speaker: narrator
text: And after it, almost lost in the dragon's breathing:

speaker: voice
text: …be patient where I was not…

speaker: narrator
text: You know it the way you know a song someone sang to you before you had words for it. Then it is gone.

speaker: narrator
text: You look up at the ancient dragon. Its golden eyes are half closed.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: The friend who stayed behind.

speaker: narrator
text: It says no more.

speaker: narrator
text: As you turn to go, the great head lowers.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: And the healer who waits at the cavern mouth. Little Mira. Tell her she has grown old.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon rumbles softly:

speaker: ancient dragon
text: The memory has been shared. The scale awaits, but it is not given for the asking. There is an old oath for it. The words are kept in the Echo Chambers.

speaker: narrator
text: ✓ In the Sunken Ruins: a letter from Aren and Lysa to their friend Malakar, begging him not to reach for time. He wrote back: You would have me wait while you die.

speaker: narrator
text: ✓ On Mount Ember: the promise the three of them burned into stone, one virtue each, and Malakar's name struck deeper than the others.

speaker: narrator
text: ✓ In the Caverns of Shadow: the dragon remembered them. They poured themselves into a ward that hides you and holds Malakar's wound shut. They are warded away, not dead.

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents were not Malakar's victims. They were his closest friends, Wardens of the Dawn like him, and when he tore at time they became the ward that hides you. The dragon says they are warded away, not dead.

speaker: narrator
text: A hall of living stone opens beyond sight, its ceiling lost in shadow. Embers burn slowly along the floor, pulsing like a heartbeat, and somewhere in the dark, water drips. Rings of old sigils spiral across the black tiles around the Ancient Dragon. It lies coiled at the centre, scales like polished obsidian, and each slow breath hums in your bones. The old dripping has stopped; from the mines beyond comes no sound of picks at all.

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues: The dragon will not give its scale for the asking. There is an old oath for it, and its words are kept in the Echo Chambers, tucked out of sight at the back of an alcove.

speaker: narrator
text: In a stone niche at the back of an alcove lies a bundle of old scrolls, tied with faded golden thread.

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues: The dragon will not give its scale for the asking. There is an old oath for it, and its words are on the old scrolls you found in the Echo Chambers. You have not read them yet.

speaker: narrator
text: Brittle parchment bound with faded golden thread. Most of the script has flaked away. One line survives, written in many hands, one beneath another: “I take what is given, and I return ___.” Each hand finished it with a word of its own, and every one of those words has worn away.

speaker: narrator
text: You have already discovered the old oath scrolls hidden in this chamber. The alcoves hold no further secrets.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold still. The whispers in the alcoves gather, and for a moment they are not copying you at all. Three voices, close and tired, as if the night they belong to never ended.

speaker: a man's voice, steady
text: Mal. Put the lamp down and listen to me.

speaker: a second man, quick and low
text: I have listened for a year, Aren. The Wasting is in Willowbrook. It is in her.

speaker: a woman's voice, hoarse
text: Then let it stay in me. Not this. Time is not a door, Mal.

speaker: the second man
text: It is only a door if I close it again.

speaker: the steady voice
text: It is a wound. You know it is. Stay. Wait with us.

speaker: the second man
text: You would have me wait while you die.

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere in the stone, a door closes. The whispers go back to copying your breath.

speaker: narrator
text: Carefully made rubbings of ancient runes containing the Resonant Chant: 'Let stillness echo, let silence bind.'

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin turns the pale stone over in his fingers. As his hand closes around it, the creak of the new braces seems to step back a pace, and his shoulders come down for the first time since you met him.

speaker: tobin
text: It's quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: His voice is a cracked whisper.

speaker: tobin
text: I could still hear it. Me, shouting. All this time, I could still hear it.

speaker: narrator
text: Across the gallery, the lead miner sets down his pick and does not pick it up again.

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin touches the charm at his throat:

speaker: tobin
text: Still quiet. I'll keep it, if that's all right. Just till we're up top.

speaker: narrator
text: The lead miner nods toward the bucket, where Tobin sits with the charm in his fist:

speaker: lead miner
text: He talked to me. Asked me how long till we're up top. First thing he's said since the rock came down.

speaker: narrator
text: He clears his throat.

speaker: lead miner
text: Thank you, Elior.

speaker: narrator
text: The phantoms turn toward you all at once. Their whispers run together, too many voices to pick one out.

speaker: narrator
text: Beneath the whispers, a few of them are humming: a slow tune that climbs three notes and settles home again.

speaker: narrator
text: Through the murmur, one word comes clear, over and over: rest … rest …

speaker: elior
text: rest

speaker: narrator
text: The whispering falters. One by one the figures turn toward you, and the hurry goes out of them. They thin until you can see the far wall through them, and then they are gone. The chamber is quieter for it, but not yet still.

speaker: narrator
text: Three weathered stones arranged in a triangle, each one carved with spiraling channels that catch and hold whispered words.

speaker: narrator
text: Obsidian water, so still it seems frozen. Yet when you lean close, the faintest tremor runs across it, too fine to see unless you are looking for it.

speaker: narrator
text: A crystal vial containing water so still it seems solid. The liquid captures and holds reflections that shouldn't be there. Tilted to the light, it shows not your face but a young woman at a long table, bent over a book, and three teachers about her: one pointing at the page, one laughing, one watching from the shadow by the door.

speaker: narrator
text: A small amulet carved from pale stone, inscribed with symbols that seem to dampen sound. It feels warm to the touch and emanates a sense of tranquility.

speaker: narrator
text: The Silence Keeper whispers:

speaker: silence keeper
text: I have kept this hush for forty years, so the sleeper below can rest. I was a singer once, in the villages above. I sang one night too loud, too near the deep, and something old turned over in its sleep. I put my voice down that night and never picked it up.

speaker: silence keeper
text: The stones in this room were cut to carry a whisper to the sleeper without waking it. They have gone cold. Bless them, and give them the old chant from the walls of the Echo Chambers, and the way will open. But a chant will not carry over troubled water, and these pools are not as still as they seem.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall figure in a deep hood stands at the water's edge. Their feet make no sound on the stone, and you find you have lowered your voice.

speaker: narrator
text: Grey figures, thin as breath on glass, move among the pools. Each does one thing over and over: lifts a hand, turns, reaches for a door that is not there. They whisper all the time.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Stillness Vestibule, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Silence Keeper does not turn:

speaker: silence keeper
text: Forty years I have listened to those stones. They are cold. Bless the stones; give them the chant. But a chant will not carry over troubled water, and these pools are not as still as they seem.

speaker: narrator
text: Oath of Stillness: Grey figures drift among the pools of the Stillness Vestibule, saying the same thing over, as they have for years. The way to the dragon's hall stays shut until the echo stones there are blessed and given the old chant. Its words are cut into the walls of the Echo Chambers.

speaker: silence keeper
text: Forty years I have listened to those stones. They are warm again. Give them the chant. But a chant will not carry over troubled water, and these pools are not as still as they seem.

speaker: narrator
text: The water lies flat as glass, holding the stones and the dark above in perfect reflection. Not a tremor crosses it.

speaker: silence keeper
text: The stones in this room were cut to carry a whisper to the sleeper without waking it. They have gone cold. Bless them, and give them the old chant from the walls of the Echo Chambers, and the way will open. The water lies true now; it will hold your words.

speaker: silence keeper
text: Forty years I have listened to those stones. They are warm again. Give them the chant. The water lies true now; it will hold your words.

speaker: narrator
text: The Silence Keeper bows their hooded head:

speaker: silence keeper
text: The stones held. The way is open, and the sleeper knows you are coming. Go quietly.

speaker: narrator
text: The sigils are cut deep, ring inside ring, and each ring glows faintly. They are the walls of the dragon's prison, and every ring holds.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: You have read the old words. Then tell me: what will you give back, for what you take?

speaker: narrator
text: A dragon lies coiled around the hall's centre. The scales along its flank are worn dull where they have pressed the floor for a very long time. Its golden eyes open slowly, and close slower.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Dragon's Hall, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: elior
text: it

speaker: elior
text: I take what is given, and I return it.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon shifts one coil, and a single scale lies loose on the tiles.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Your words ring true, young one. It is heavier than it looks.

speaker: elior
text: I take what is given, and I return myself.

speaker: elior
text: what I take

speaker: elior
text: I take what is given, and I return what I take.

speaker: narrator
text: A mysterious amulet inscribed with runes. At its centre is the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn: the sun rising over three linked rings. In its depths Aren and Lysa stand hand in hand. The third figure keeps his back turned.

speaker: elior
text: everything

speaker: elior
text: I take what is given, and I return everything.

speaker: narrator
text: A scale from the dragon, dark as midnight and shot through with veins of deep gold. It is cold, and heavier than it looks.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: You have said it. The scale is there, young one. Take it.

speaker: narrator
text: The scale is cold, and heavier than it looks. You take its weight in both hands.

speaker: narrator
text: You have the dragon's scale, heavy in your pack. With all three relics in hand, Mira's Warding Rite is all that is left.

speaker: narrator
text: Light runs along the cracked ring like water finding its course. The sigils brighten, steady, and hold.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon lowers its head.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: You said you would give back. Most forget by the time they reach the door. Your parents would not have forgotten.

speaker: narrator
text: A hall of living stone opens beyond sight, its ceiling lost in shadow. Embers burn slowly along the floor, pulsing like a heartbeat, and somewhere in the dark, water drips. Rings of old sigils spiral across the black tiles around the Ancient Dragon. It lies coiled at the centre, scales like polished obsidian, and each slow breath hums in your bones. The old dripping has stopped; from the mines beyond comes no sound of picks at all. The sigils around the dragon burn steady and whole again.

speaker: narrator
text: The nearest ring is whole again, its sigils glowing like the rest. The prison holds.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Go with my blessing, young one. The prison holds.

speaker: narrator
text: The crack splits the nearest ring clean through, and the sigils on either side of it have gone dull. The prison is weaker than it was.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Go with my blessing. The prison I hold is weaker for the scale's going. That is the price, and it is mine to pay, not yours.

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues: You have the dragon's scale, heavy in your pack. With all three relics in hand, Mira's Warding Rite is all that is left.

speaker: narrator
text: A hall of living stone opens beyond sight, its ceiling lost in shadow. Embers burn slowly along the floor, pulsing like a heartbeat, and somewhere in the dark, water drips. Rings of old sigils spiral across the black tiles around the Ancient Dragon. It lies coiled at the centre, scales like polished obsidian, and each slow breath hums in your bones. The old dripping has stopped; from the mines beyond comes no sound of picks at all. Where the scale lay, the sigils around the dragon have dimmed, and a crack splits the nearest ring clean through.

speaker: silence keeper
text: The sleeper spoke with you, and the stone held. Forty years, and I have never been so glad to have kept a quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: The Mine Overseer counts heads under his breath, and gets the same number twice.

speaker: mine overseer
text: All of them. Even the boy.

speaker: narrator
text: He lets go of the arch at last.

speaker: narrator
text: You give her the dragon's words. Mira does not answer.

speaker: mira
text: That is all three. Now we go home, to my hut, and I make them into something the king can use.

speaker: mira
text: The king is fading, Elior. We have less time than I hoped.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric looks at his hands.

speaker: sir cedric
text: He was taken on my watch. He will not die on it.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira's hands stop above the three relics. She does not begin the rite.

speaker: mira
text: Before I bind them, Elior, there is something you must hear from me, and not from a stone or a dragon.

speaker: mira
text: You noticed. I saw you notice.

speaker: mira
text: I knew your parents. Not as a healer knows a neighbour. I was their pupil — Aren's, Lysa's, and Malakar's. The three of them taught me everything I know of circles and wards.

speaker: mira
text: When Aren and Lysa poured themselves into the ward, someone had to stay with the child it hid. I came to Willowbrook as its healer, and I have watched over you every day since.

speaker: mira
text: Your grandmother knew. She is Lysa's mother, and she kept the secret with me.

speaker: narrator
text: For a moment you cannot speak. Then the words come out harder than you meant them.

speaker: elior
text: Why didn't you tell me?

speaker: mira
text: Because the seal could not bear it. Malakar's cloaked agent walked Willowbrook's lanes searching for the amulet, and any word of who you were could have reached him.

speaker: mira
text: Lyria wrote to me from Greendale, about a girl with a curse no one could lift. I burned the letter. If I had gone, I would have shown Greendale what the healer at Willowbrook can do, with his agent in both towns and you in one of them. I have never been so ashamed of anything.

speaker: mira
text: I am telling you now because you have earned the truth. The amulet you carry is the anchor of the ward your parents became.

speaker: mira
text: Say what you need to say to me, Elior. I would rather hear it now.

speaker: narrator
text: (Answer her with: say i forgive you or say you should have told me to Mira.)

speaker: narrator
text: She looks down at the relics, and then back at you.

speaker: mira
text: When you are ready, tell me, and I will begin the Warding Rite.

speaker: mira
text: And ask me anything you like now — about your parents, Malakar, the amulet, your grandmother. I will not hide from you again.

speaker: mira
text: The three relics resonate, Elior. Listen. They were made together, and they know it.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira sets the three relics in a triangle on her table and draws a chalk circle round them, the way she drew the one in the castle yard. The crystal flares white. The feather catches fire and does not burn. The scale hums.

speaker: narrator
text: She takes the healing herbs from the shelf and presses the sachets into your hands. They smell of resin, and your breath slows while the circle tightens.

speaker: narrator
text: She says three words under her breath, and the chalk lines go dark one after another.

speaker: narrator
text: The relics soften at the edges, run together like wax, and are gone. On the table where they stood is a small glass vial the colour of first light: the lifelight elixir.

speaker: mira
text: It is done. This can stop what he is doing to the king. Take it, and tell me when you are ready for the fortress.

speaker: mira
text: The elixir, Elior. You must take the lifelight elixir before we depart. I did not make it to leave it on my table.

speaker: elior
text: forgive

speaker: narrator
text: Mira closes her eyes. For a moment she looks younger, and very tired.

speaker: mira
text: Thank you. I did not dare ask for that. I will try to deserve it.

speaker: elior
text: you should have told me

speaker: narrator
text: Mira does not look away.

speaker: mira
text: I should have. I chose the seal over you every day, and I would choose it again. But I am sorry for every one of those days.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Do what she needs, Elior. I have waited this long. I can wait one more hour.

speaker: narrator
text: Low on one facet, almost lost in the light, someone has scratched a seven with a bar through it. Lysa's hand. Your mother cut this prism.

speaker: narrator
text: The village healer — and, you know now, the Wardens' pupil, who stayed in Willowbrook for your sake. She meets your eyes more easily than before.

speaker: narrator
text: Main quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: You have completed the quest 'The Three Virtues'.

speaker: narrator
text: A small glass vial the colour of first light. Something moves in it: a white glint, a thread of flame, a dark shimmer like a scale turning. Mira made it from the three relics, to stop what Malakar is doing to the king.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Then it is the fortress. I have been walking toward that door since the night he was taken.

speaker: mira
text: Then this is the final journey. Malakar's fortress.

speaker: mira
text: I know the road. I walked it as a girl, when it was the Wardens' hall and not his fortress. Your parents made the relics there, at a workbench under the dome.

speaker: mira
text: It is the longest circle I have ever drawn. Stay close when we land.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric stands looking up at the gates.

speaker: sir cedric
text: If I had held the door that night, we would not be standing at this one.

speaker: narrator
text: Words carved beneath the runes of a sunlit glade come back to you.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira leans on the cold stone of the gate. Her hands are still shaking from the last circle.

speaker: mira
text: I know how I look, Elior. Do not ask me to stay behind.

speaker: mira
text: Your parents walked into the dark without me once. I will not let you do the same. I am coming with you.

speaker: mira
text: I am right behind you, Elior. The gates will not open themselves.

speaker: elior
text: refrain

speaker: elior
text: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric is quiet. Then he nods, once, and loosens his sword in its sheath.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Truth, then. The truth is I was on the wall. The truth is he is still alive. Let us go and get him.

speaker: narrator
text: Entrance to Malakar's Fortress

speaker: narrator
text: A bastion of black stone rises from a shattered ridge. Iron lattices close its gates, and sigils glow behind them, slow as breathing. The wind up here is cold and smells of metal. Where the gate arch meets the wall an older carving shows through the black: a sun rising over three linked rings.

speaker: narrator
text: The gates are taller than a house, and the sigils on them seem to move at the edge of sight. Beyond the lattice, corridors run into the dark. Somewhere in there is King Alden.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient amulet is warm against your palm. You came on this journey believing Malakar took your parents from you. You know better now. Aren and Lysa were his closest friends, and the ward they became is still holding.

speaker: narrator
text: The Dragon said they were warded away, not dead. You do not yet know what that means.

speaker: narrator
text: In your pack, the lifelight elixir is warm. Act III is complete. The final confrontation awaits.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Entrance to Malakar's Fortress, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Act III complete. Trials and Revelations.

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents were Malakar's closest friends. The Dragon says they are warded away, not dead.

speaker: narrator
text: One of the phantoms stops in front of you and says something very fast, the same few words three times over. You do not catch them. It moves on and starts again.

speaker: narrator
text: The phantoms drift closer. Their mouths move a moment behind their whispers, like an echo running the wrong way.

speaker: narrator
text: One of the phantoms reaches for a door that is not there, opens it, and reaches for it again. The others whisper on around it.
